status: Frozen before this round's results; adaptive research on previously inspected history, not an untouched holdout
question: Can bounded dip buying or holding positive trends outperform both SPY and gold without the original grid's drawdown?
primary_reason: Diversification, trend exits and volatility sizing have prior published motivation; this is a different strategy from the TikTok grid
warmup: 2019 gold quotes; all candidates and benchmarks start together in 2020 or 2022
signals: Previous completed US-session close only; orders at next session open; weekly rules rebalance on first session of each ISO week
gold_execution: Funded gold spot proxy with 0.4% annual holding drag, not the earlier fully financed CFD; portfolio prices sampled at US open/close from minute bid/ask midpoints
spy_execution: Existing split/dividend-adjusted daily OHLC, with dividends implicitly reinvested; fractional units allowed
dip_rules: Above 200-session average: buy 50% of capped exposure; add 25% on each of up to two further 20-session ATR close-to-close drops. Quantity based on current equity; never double. Sell next open after close falls below average, basket equity loses 5%, or optional net gain per gold unit exceeds one entry ATR. After a loss wait 20 sessions. Trim exposure at next open if prior close exceeds cap. No intraday guaranteed stop.
trend_rules: Positive means close above trailing moving average. Gold-only holds while positive. Vol-scaled rules size using trailing 60-session covariance, target 15% annualized volatility, cap gross exposure. Diversified rule inverse-vol weights eligible gold/SPY; relative rule holds eligible asset with highest 126-session return. Rebalance weekly; no shorts.
controls_rules: Unleveraged single-asset controls buy and hold. Mix and leveraged single assets rebalance monthly. Same trade, gold holding and borrowing assumptions.
pass_rule: Higher after-cost ending equity than BOTH unleveraged benchmarks in BOTH start periods, daily-close drawdown <=25% in BOTH, and no reliance solely on leverage versus same-cap mix. This is a research screen, not confidence of future outperformance.

robustness.annual_walk_forward: Starting 2023, choose among the 11 fixed strategies using only 2020 through previous December: highest CAGR among positive-return rules with <=25% close drawdown, else cash. Do not describe reused history as untouched.

limitations: No historical taxes or broker-specific availability
Gold fund proxy is not a traded ETF history
No modern LLM asked to predict historical prices from hindsight
